title: The citation that pointed at nothing
blurb: Offsets were never verified and an update silently re-pointed old citations.
prompt: A generated answer cited a quote that no longer existed, because the draft stored offsets without checking them and resolved by document id, so an update re-pointed every old citation at new text. The same store marked fetch failures valid. Review it, fix it, and prove spans resolve against immutable versions.
aiNote: The draft stores caller-provided offsets without validating them against the document bytes, and its cache and resolution key by document id instead of (document, version), so a document update silently rewrites what old citations point at.
testIdea: Submit an offset whose bytes do not match the quote and assert 422; update the document and assert an old citation still resolves against its version; time out the fetch and assert broken status, not valid.
followUps: How would you re-anchor a citation after a small edit?
What TTL makes sense for span caches of immutable versions?
Should an answer with one broken citation fail the whole response?
